source: PSR Discord 'Gen 1 Resources' pins 'Red TID' (Drive 1LfZfZnYwIeF4HL2RnwFBl_TjaFzv_tUA) and 'Yellow TID List' (Drive 1NeHnA070djPBJJ5ht7X1yimAIrPCw3zL), files dated 2018-03-24, decoded against pret pokered/pokeyellow and reproduced on pokemon-speedrunning/gambatte-core (GBP mode, GBC boot ROM); Blue and the DMG tables are derived on the same core. 's' = centiseconds from power-on to the Trainer ID roll on the emulator (list-only rows: community Offset minus 1.644 s Red / 1.660 s Yellow). 'v': b = list row reproduced by the harness, h = derived only, l = community row not run here (reset-family rows are sampled, not run exhaustively). Entries per TID are best-first: reset-free, then fewest tokens, then lowest seconds.
frame_convention: harness step index after power-on (see windows.note); seconds_per_frame = 70224/4194304 for LCD frames; game_start_frame / nintendo_logo_frame per platform anchor a practice timeline ('tap when the Nintendo logo appears')

tokens.digit: a bare digit 0-6 is hopN (Red/Blue) or introN (Yellow); hop6 = 6, introwait = i
tokens.implicit: every sequence ends in newgame, which is not encoded (e encodes a newgame in the middle of a reset chain, e.g. ..._newgame_oakreset_...)

encoding.entry: seq code (tokens above) | s = 3 base36 chars, centiseconds from power-on to the Trainer ID roll | v = one char: b (community-list row reproduced by the harness), h (harness-derived only), l (community-list row not run here) | w = for v in {b,h}: 4 base36 chars per title token of the sequence (2 chars reg, 2 chars exit, each minus the bounds' minimum in windows.<game>.<platform>.scenes.title.<token>) - nothing for v = l
encoding.pack: games.<game>.<platform>.packed: ids = null when all 65536 IDs are present (entry groups are in TID order 0..65535), else base36 deltas joined by ',' (first = TID, then TID - previous - 1); seqs = entry groups joined by ';' (one group per TID, in TID order), entries in a group joined by '|'; s, v, w = concatenated per entry in that same order (fixed widths, no separators; w has 4 chars per title token of the decoded sequence and 0 chars for v = l)
encoding.decode: split seqs on ';' -> groups (TID from ids or the group index); split a group on '|' -> entries; for each entry in order: decode the code (see tokens), take the next 3 chars of s (base36 -> centiseconds), the next char of v, and if v != 'l' the next 4*(number of title tokens) chars of w
encoding.timeline:
compose_timeline(): frame = platforms.

.game_start_frame + windows.gamefreak_start; for each action in order: scene entries give reg (the poll where the press registers) and next (the next scene start), both relative to the scene start; title actions take reg/exit from w; opt(backout) is two actions (opt in the main menu, opt-exit in the option menu), opt(reset) likewise (opt, opt-reset); newgame's roll = reg + roll_delay

nopal.means: Touch nothing while the Nintendo logo is on screen after power-on (about the first 2.5 s). Any button pressed in that window changes the ID.
nopal.window: boot frames 12-145 after power-on (0.20-2.43 s) must see no input; the game starts at frame 186 (3.13 s)
nopal.citation: cgb_boot.bin joypad polling during the logo (measured: a press in frames 12-145 changes the ID, frames 0-10 and 146+ do not)

pal.means: Hold a direction (Up, Down, Left or Right; all four give the same ID) from power-on, then let go while the logo is still on screen.
pal.window: direction down by boot frame 84 (1.41 s) at the latest and released between frames 12 and 144 (0.20-2.41 s); a single 2-frame tap inside 12-84 is enough
pal.citation: cgb_boot.bin palette selection (direction + optional A/B during the logo); measured windows

pal(hold).means: Hold a direction from power-on and keep holding it until the game has started (past the end of the logo).
pal(hold).window: direction down by boot frame 84 (1.41 s) and still down at frame 146 (2.44 s); release any time after that and before the first Game Freak-logo poll (8.7 s) - before it if the next token is gfreset
pal(hold).citation: cgb_boot.bin; measured: releases at frames >= 146 all give the pal(hold) ID

nopal(ab).means: Press A or B (no direction) at any time while the Nintendo logo is on screen; a tap is enough.
nopal(ab).window: A or B down at some frame in 12-144 (0.20-2.41 s); held or tapped, same ID

pal(ab).means: Hold a direction from power-on and, about 1.2-1.4 s after power-on, also press A or B and keep both held until the game starts.
pal(ab).window: direction down from frame <= 8 through frame 146+; A or B pressed in frames 70-85 (1.17-1.42 s) and held to game start. Earlier A/B presses give one of three IDs depending on (frame mod 6): not humanly reliable

gfskip.means: Hold Up+Select+B (or A, or START) before the Game Freak shooting-star logo appears; the logo is skipped at its first poll.
gfskip.window: any time after the boot finishes (3.13 s) and before the first shooting-star poll (frame 519, 8.69 s after power-on = frame 333 after game start); the press registers at that poll. Which button does not change the ID unless hop0 follows (then Up+Select+B must stay held, see hop0)
gfskip.citation: pokered engine/movie/splash.asm:50 (AnimateShootingStar, ld c,1 / call CheckForUserInterruption); home/overworld.asm:2395-2424 CheckForUserInterruption

gfwait.means: Do not touch anything during the Game Freak logo; let it play out.
gfwait.window: no START/A press (and Up+Select+B not held) during the 214 polling frames of the shooting star (game frames 333-546)
gfwait.citation: pokered engine/movie/splash.asm:27-146; intro.asm:325-331 (40-frame delay after the animation only when not interrupted)

gfreset.means: Hold A+B+Select+Start before the Game Freak logo; the game soft-resets from the logo (16 frames after the first poll) and the sequence continues from the copyright screen (no boot ROM, so no palette token).
gfreset.window: combo down before the first shooting-star poll, held until the screen goes white (SoftReset); no direction may be held (the check is for exactly A+B+Select+Start)
gfreset.citation: pokered engine/joypad.asm:5-7,50-60 (_Joypad: cp PAD_BUTTONS -> TrySoftReset, hSoftReset=16 polls); home/init.asm:1-6 SoftReset

hopN.means: Press A (or START) during the Nidorino/Gengar scene so that it registers at the start of the N-th polling window: hop0 = the walk-in, hop1..hop5 = the pauses after the 1st, 2nd, 3rd (post-slash), 4th and 5th hops. hop0 directly after gfskip is NOT a new press: keep Up+Select+B held from the Game Freak skip into the scene. hop6 = do nothing, the scene plays out.
hopN.window: press during the non-polling animation before the window (hip/hop animations use DelayFrames, no joypad read): the press registers at the window's first poll. Windows (frames after PlayIntroScene): 1-80, 131-140, 191-274, 300-397, 448-467, 488-517; gaps between them 50, 50, 25, 50, 20 frames
hopN.citation: pokered engine/movie/intro.asm:23-141 (PlayIntroScene: IntroMoveMon c=2 x40, CheckForUserInterruption c=10/30/30/30/60/20/30; AnimateIntroNidorino DelayFrames c=5); home/overworld.asm:2395

hop6.means: Do nothing. Let the Nidorino/Gengar scene play out to its end - hop6 is the do-nothing member of the hop family, not a sixth press.
hop6.window: no A/START press and no Up+Select+B held for the whole scene
hop6.citation: pokered engine/movie/intro.asm:135-141 (the lunge, then the return, with no CheckForUserInterruption after)

hopN(reset).means: Same window as hopN but hold A+B+Select+Start instead; soft reset 16 frames later.

titleN.means: Press START (or A) so that it registers at the first poll of the (N+1)-th title-screen window (N = how many Pokemon have scrolled in after the first): title0 = during the title's build-up (logo bounce, version scroll), before the first poll.
titleN.window: press during the non-polling part: title0 = the 150 frames from the title screen start to its first poll; titleN = during the ball animation / new-Pokemon load after the N-th scroll-in. Each window polls for 200 frames
titleN.citation: pokered engine/movie/title.asm:149-237 (bounce, 36-frame delay, version scroll, .awaitUserInterruptionLoop ld c,200); title2.asm:19-83 TitleScroll (rLY busy-wait, no joypad)

titleN(scroll).means: Press START (or A) while the (N+1)-th Pokemon is scrolling in: it registers at the single poll right after the scroll.
titleN(scroll).window: the 17-frame scroll-in (TitleScreenScrollInMon) after the N-th 200-frame window; registers at the ld c,1 CheckForUserInterruption

titleN(reset).means: As titleN but hold A+B+Select+Start (soft reset).

titleN(usb).means: As titleN but hold Up+Select+B: the title exits into the 'Clear all saved data?' dialog; csreset must follow.

csreset.means: At the clear-save dialog hold A+B+Select+Start (soft reset).
csreset.window: any time before the dialog's first poll (the text print)

opt(backout).means: At the main menu hold Down+A (Down+START also works) before the menu polls: OPTION opens; then hold START (or B) so the option menu closes at its first poll.
opt(backout).window: Down+A down during the 20-frame delay + draw before HandleMenuInput_'s first poll; START/B down during the 20-frame delay + draw before DisplayOptionMenu's first poll
opt(backout).citation: pokered engine/menus/main_menu.asm:13-90 (.mainMenuLoop, HandleMenuInput, DisplayOptionMenu), :483-502 (.getJoypadStateLoop); home/window.asm:5-108 HandleMenuInput_

opt(reset).means: Open OPTION as in opt(backout), then hold A+B+Select+Start in the option menu.

backout.means: At the main menu hold B before it polls: back to the title screen (the title build-up replays, then titleN applies again).
backout.window: B down during the 20-frame delay + draw before the menu's first poll

ngreset.means: At the main menu hold A+B+Select+Start (soft reset from NEW GAME).

newgame.means: At the main menu hold A (or START) before it polls: NEW GAME. The Trainer ID is rolled 30 frames later (29 in Yellow) in Oak's speech.
newgame.window: A down during the 20-frame delay + draw before HandleMenuInput_'s first poll (registers at that poll)
newgame.citation: pokered engine/menus/main_menu.asm:68-86 -> StartNewGame; engine/movie/oak_speech/oak_speech.asm:42-52 (predef InitPlayerData2); engine/movie/oak_speech/init_player_data.asm:1-10 (two Random calls); engine/math/random.asm (rDIV)

oakreset.means: After NEW GAME, hold A+B+Select+Start during Oak's speech (soft reset); the ID is rolled again by the next newgame.
oakreset.window: before the first text-print poll of Oak's speech

introN.means: Yellow: press A (or START/B) so that it registers at the first poll of the N-th Pikachu-intro scene start (scene changes with the screen blanked); introwait = let the whole intro play.
introN.window: press during the 7-9 blank frames before scene N's first poll; the intro polls every frame otherwise
introN.citation: pokeyellow engine/movie/intro_yellow.asm:12-30 (JoypadLowSensitivity each loop, hJoyPressed & A|B|START), YellowIntro_BlankPalsDelay2AndDisableLCD

title.means: Yellow: press START (or A) during the title build-up so it registers at the title loop's first poll (Yellow's title has one window; no scroll).
title.window: the ~150 non-polling frames from the title start to .titleScreenLoop's first poll

gbp.name: GBA silicon (Game Boy Player, GBA/GBA SP, GSE or gambatte-speedrun GBP mode) with the GBC boot ROM
gbp.status: emulator-exact: pokemon-speedrunning/gambatte-core CGB_MODE|GBA_FLAG with cgb_boot.bin reproduces the community Red list on 1,132,014 of its 1,132,015 rows (every published sequence was run on 2026-09-16; the one disagreement is pal_gfskip_hop0_title1(scroll)_opt(backout)_backout_title3_newgame, community 6BA3 vs harness 749A, timings agree, cause unresolved) and the Yellow list on all 183,478 rows; plain GBC mode (CGB_MODE without GBA_FLAG) reproduces 0/30, so the lists are GBP-mode lists. Not hardware-validated.

dmg.name: original Game Boy (DMG boot ROM)
dmg.status: derived on the same core with the DMG boot ROM and the same grammar (no palette tokens: the DMG boot has none); no community list exists for it and it is not hardware-validated.

windows.note: per game and platform: the windows model measured with `bufferderive windows` over every CSV row (windows_model.py); frames are harness steps after power-on (0-based; a step is one LCD frame of 70224 cycles except that a step ends early at every LCD on/off, so step counts run ahead of LCD frames by one per LCD switch; times in seconds (reg_s, next_s: means over the measured rows, spread <= time_spread_ms_max) are exact emulator time). Scene frame 0 = the frame the scene routine is entered (AnimateShootingStar, PlayIntroScene, DisplayTitleScreen, MainMenu.mainMenuLoop, DisplayOptionMenu, DoClearSaveDialogue, OakSpeech). gap = first frame of the press window relative to the scene start (0 = the window opens before the scene, at the previous action's registered poll + 1: no poll lies in between), reg = the poll at which the press registers, next = [scene, frame] the next scene starts, run = the poll run a skip-only action lets pass, run_last = last poll of a reset token's run (SoftReset fires 16 polls after the press). Title actions (Red/Blue titleN*, Yellow title*) are NOT constants: the title Pokemon are random and each one's sprite load and cry take a different number of frames, and the title's rLY busy-waits round differently by sub-frame phase (Yellow: one frame by entry path); their entries hold min/max bounds and every harness entry carries its own measured reg/exit in w. Reset-family tokens: measured on the validation rows; a soft reset re-enters the Game Freak scene next.

boot.note: boot-ROM (palette) tokens have absolute windows in harness steps after power-on; the CGB boot ROM polls the pad during the Nintendo logo (README 'The grammar'); they do not change any later frame

dmg.note: the DMG boot ROM reads no input: no palette tokens

red-2swap.name: Any% 2-swap: TID high byte $40
red-2swap.route: the corruption's second swap is an 11-byte offset-preserving copy that lands ($D358, the Trainer ID's HIGH byte) in wCurMapScriptPtr with bank $1D mapped, so the jump target is $HH01 and $1D:$4001 is inside the map-block data that runs as a sled into HallOfFamePC at $1D:$405C. Swap 1 (party slots 7<->21) overwrites $D35A-$D364 and destroys the Trainer ID's LOW byte before swap 2 runs, so only the high byte reaches the pointer: every $4000-$40FF is route-valid, 1 in 256, and no $40xx is a trap
red-2swap.provenance: EMPIRICAL (emulator, 2026-09-04, Red): all 256 Trainer IDs $4000-$40FF, each driven through the documented 15-step button sequence with no forced PC and no poked menu variables, reach HallOfFamePC on frame 1472 with HL = $4001 at the 'jp hl' in RunMapScript; the Trainer ID read back after swap 1 is $4000 on every row. Isolation control on the same state: forcing $D358 to $AD gives jump $40AD and a hard lock, while Trainer ID $40AD reaches the Hall of Fame. Reproduced on a third corrupted save minted by gambatte-core from a genuine NEW GAME plus mid-save reset; an exhaustive search over all 65,280 swap index pairs finds no 1- or 2-swap path from $D35A to $D36E/$D36F. WITHDRAWN 2026-09-04: the earlier low-byte window $00-$38 / $3A-$5C (and its $39 hole) came from sweeps that poison the Trainer ID and poke wCurMapScriptPtr directly - column 5 of sled_blue_40.csv is the pointer low byte, not a Trainer ID low byte - so it constrains the JUMP POINTER and still governs the separate TID-free route, not this one. UNCONFIRMED ON HARDWARE: every measurement here is emulator work (PyBoy for the runs, gambatte-core for the saves and the hold tables); the claim is WRAM arithmetic rather than timing, so it should transfer, but no cartridge run has been done. INFERRED for Blue: $1D:$4000-$405B is byte-identical in pokeblue.gbc and the swap code is the same source, but no Blue corruption-route sweep was run. STRUCTURAL: pret/pokered bank $1D map-block data before HallOfFamePC.

psr-64c2.name: PSR Red/Blue Any% route: 'Manip TID 64C2 (25794)', the one published target
psr-64c2.route: the Trainer ID bytes become wCurMapScriptPtr in bank $16 after the save corruption; the route's swap list is written for 64C2 and no other value
psr-64c2.provenance: EMPIRICAL: the PSR route README (pokemon-speedrunning routes docs/gen-1/red-blue/main-any/README.md, 2026-09-02) names exactly one target, 'Manip TID 64C2 (25794)', with its swap list. $64C2 occurs in NO table under the hold-START methodologies (Red, Blue; offsets 0-5999), so a runner of that route should not expect this tool to reach it; the other bank-$16 values prior searches accepted are the separate, opt-in set bank16-family-inferred.

bank16-family-inferred.name: bank-$16 family {$64BD, $64BE, $64C1, $64C6} that the owner's prior route searches accepted (INFERRED: no published swap list)
bank16-family-inferred.route: INFERRED: each of these lands wCurMapScriptPtr in the same bank-$16 region as 64C2, but the PSR swap list is for 64C2 only; a member needs its own item-swap list, which nobody has published
bank16-family-inferred.provenance: INFERRED from ~/AI/speedrun-research/RESEARCH.md round-4 section 5.6 (the bank-$16 destinations prior searches accepted) - a working directory on the author's machine, in NEITHER REPOSITORY and not committed, so nothing shipped here shows that search; this set rests on that note alone. Not route-valid for the PSR route as written: applying the 64C2 swap list to a 64BD save is not known to work. Red tables: $64BD at GBA offset 1084 and DMG offset 721 (one derivation each); no member in Blue's tables (offsets 0-5999).

psr-yellow.name: PSR Yellow Any% route: 'Manip TID 6415 (25621) or 64EA (25834)'
psr-yellow.route: 64EA saves 16 frames later in the run but is harder to hit; the item swap differs (TM34 -> Carbos instead of Boulderbadge -> Carbos)
psr-yellow.provenance: EMPIRICAL: the PSR route README (docs/gen-1/yellow/main-any/README.md, 2026-09-02): 'Manip TID: 6415 (25621) or 64EA (25834); this manip saves 16 frames later into the run, but it's harder to pull off'. Under yellow/*/hold-start-v1 neither ID occurs in offsets 0-5999 on either boot; 64EA occurs only under an after-intro hold on the DMG (START held from frames 2093-2305, menu 2360, offset 2005), not shipped as a methodology; 6415 was not found under any of the three Yellow plateaus swept (docs/FACTS.md).
